title: Blockwise attention microkernel with in-place rotary + KV coalescing
author: Asha Mehta
description:
Motivation: reduce per-token compute and memory pressure for mixed-length workloads by introducing a blockwise attention microkernel that applies rotary embeddings in-place and a coalesced KV slab layout to reduce eviction churn under continuous batching. This is targeted at production inference workloads where many short requests interleave with occasional long sequences, and where KV cache eviction/compaction hurts tail latency and throughput.

Design summary: single-string overview of the changes and rationale. The change introduces: 1) a blockwise attention microkernel (C++/CUDA) that operates on fixed tiles (configurable tile sizes per-device) and performs matmul, rotary application, and softmax reduction across tiles to improve register reuse and reduce intermediate memory traffic; 2) in-place rotary application baked into the microkernel so we avoid an extra QKV transform buffer and extra memcopies for rotary/rope, enabling a fused Q*K pass for short sequences; 3) a coalesced slab layout for KV cache where cache entries are allocated in device slabs grouped by model-shard and sequence-block to reduce fragmentation and avoid frequent small reallocations; 4) scheduler hints to prefer homogenous micro-batches (same tile shapes) and a lightweight placement heuristic that pins streams to slots with matching slab affinity; 5) an opt-in runtime flag redwood.runtime.attn.blockwise_enabled and a dynamic tunable redwood.runtime.attn.tile_size that defaults to 64 for A100/B100 families but is auto-tuned during warmup.

What changed (high level):
- Serving runtime: new kernel registration and selection path for blockwise_attn (kernel selector picks blockwise_attn when model architecture and sequence distribution fit heuristics).
- Kernels: new CUDA microkernel (src/serving/kernels/blockwise_attn.cu) and a small CPU fallback (src/serving/kernels/blockwise_attn_cpu.cc).
- KV cache: allocator and layout changes (src/serving/kv/coalesced_slab.h, .cc) plus eviction policy tweaks to prefer LRU within slab groups.
- Scheduler: runtime/router updates to emit tile-shaped batch groups (src/serving/scheduler/tile_grouping.{cc,h}) and added placement hints in request metadata.
- Config/flags: runtime config and console flags for tuning.

Benchmarks (perf-lab A100, end-to-end inference with standard chat workload and continuous-batching enabled):
- Seq=128, batch mix skewed to short: throughput +1.9x, median latency -22%, p95 latency -18%.
- Seq=512, mixed: throughput +1.4x, p95 -11%.
- Seq=4096 (long): p95 latency -12% due to reduced KV eviction stalls when long sequences interleave.
- Token/dollar improvement measured at 1.45x on our internal cost model for typical production mix.

Safety / compatibility: feature gated behind redwood.runtime.attn.blockwise_enabled=false by default for private/dedicated until validated per-customer. The API surface (generation/embeddings endpoints) is unchanged: kernel selection is internal. Backwards compatible with pinned model-versions and will not run when a model requires a kernel not supported by blockwise_attn (e.g., certain fused custom ops).

Testing and validation:
- Unit tests for slab allocator and eviction (tests/kv/coalesced_slab_test.cc).
- Microbench harness added under perf/bench/blockwise_attn_bench.cc with autotest runs on perf-canary.
- Integration smoke tests in CI: python-sdk functional tests and a reduced perf-smoke were run; perf smoke was flaky once but the rerun passed.
- End-to-end perf runs recorded in perf-lab and uploaded as artifacts (perf-lab job IDs in comments).

Checklist: [x] Kernel correctness tests [x] Bench harness added [x] Perf regression guard rails [x] Feature flag + config [x] Documentation: docs/ops/blockwise_attn.md added (usage, tradeoffs, tuning guidance) [x] Rollout plan: staged canary -> dedicated pool opt-in -> wider default.

Changed files (high level): list of key files modified and purpose. Small illustrative snippets included only where helpful.

Related tickets and context: Linear: ENG-4892 (continuous-batching KV eviction reduction), ENG-5031 (kernel selector improvements). Also follows up on earlier work on fused rotary/flash integration but purposely uses a simpler, narrower microkernel to increase robustness and support a broader range of models.

Merge: squash-merged after perf lab artifacts matched expectations and two approvals.

Notes for reviewers: pay special attention to memory ordering in coalesced_slab and the fallback slow path correctness. Tuning knobs are intentionally conservative; we expect incremental future improvements (auto-tiling, int8 kernels).

release_notes: Introduces a blockwise attention microkernel with in-place rotary application and a coalesced KV slab cache layout. Provides up to ~1.9x throughput improvement on short-sequence heavy mixes and lower tail latency for mixed workloads. Feature is behind a runtime flag and opt-in for Dedicated/Private until fully validated.
